name_en: Mohamed Salah Qeshta محمد صلاح قشطة
full_name_ar: محمد صلاح قشطة He was killed along with two other journalists in an occupation bombing that targeted a car in Madinat al-Zahraa in the central Gaza Strip, where he was on a filming mission for the Egyptian Committee camps in the central Gaza Strip. An Israeli airstrike hit a vehicle clearly marked with the emblem of the Egyptian Committee in the Al-Zahraa area of central Gaza. The vehicle was carrying journalists and staff who were on an assignment documenting Egypt’s humanitarian work and newly established refugee tent camps in the Netzarim corridor. The Journalist Abdel Raouf Shaat was killed instantly alonside two other journalists, Mohammed Salah Qashta and Anas Ghneim. The journalists were in a vehicle displaying the Egyptian Committee’s logo, known to both local sources and, reportedly, to the Israeli military. The attack occurred despite a ceasefire, and video of the charred wreckage circulated online. Local and international media watchdogs have raised concerns about the targeting of journalists during the conflict. Medical officials said the bodies of two journalists were taken to Shifa Hospital in Gaza City, while the third was taken to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah. Civil Defense spokesman Mahmoud Basal said, "The journalists were performing a field photography mission in Netzarim (using a drone), while documenting the conditions of camps supervised by the Egyptian committee". He added that the journalists were wearing distinctive press clothing while they were at the targeting site. According to the Committee to Protect Journalists, Qeshta worked as a spokesperson for the Egyptian Committee for Gaza Relief and also reported news to a large following on Telegram, indicating he was an active and connected reporter within Palestinian media circles      .

full_name_ar: عبد الرؤوف شعت
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Full Name : Abdul Raouf Samir Shaat | عبد الرؤوف سمير شعت He was killed 13 days after his wedding with two other journalists in an Israeli drone strike that targeted a car in Madinat Al-Zahraa in the central Gaza Strip, where he was on a filming mission for the Egyptian Committee camps in the central Gaza Strip. An Israeli airstrike hit a vehicle clearly marked with the emblem of the Egyptian Committee in the Al-Zahraa area of central Gaza. The vehicle was carrying journalists and staff who were on an assignment documenting Egypt’s humanitarian work and newly established refugee tent camps in the Netzarim corridor. The Journalist Abdel Raouf Shaat was killed instantly alonside two other journalists, Mohammed Salah Qashta and Anas Ghneim. The journalists were in a vehicle displaying the Egyptian Committee’s logo, known to both local sources and, reportedly, to the Israeli military. The attack occurred despite a ceasefire, and video of the charred wreckage circulated online. Local and international media watchdogs have raised concerns about the targeting of journalists during the conflict. Medical officials said the bodies of two journalists were taken to Shifa Hospital in Gaza City, while the third was taken to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah. Civil Defense spokesman Mahmoud Basal said, "The journalists were performing a field photography mission in Netzarim (using a drone), while documenting the conditions of camps supervised by the Egyptian committee". He added that the journalists were wearing distinctive press clothing while they were at the targeting site. The Israel Defense Forces released a spin saying troops "identified several suspects who operated a drone affiliated with Hamas in the central Gaza Strip, in a manner that posed a threat to their safety," and then "struck the suspects who activated the drone." Abdel Raouf Shaat was a Palestinian freelance photo and video journalist who regularly contributed to Agence France-Presse (AFP). Although he was not on an AFP assignment at the time of the strike, colleagues and the agency described him as a deeply committed journalist and a valued member of the press community covering Gaza. AFP issued a statement mourning his death and calling for a full investigation, emphasizing his professional dedication and the danger faced by journalists in Gaza. He had also worked for years as a photographer for CBS News and other outlets. Friends and fellow journalists noted that just weeks before his death he had been congratulated on his recent wedding, highlighting the personal tragedy of his loss      .

full_name_ar: محمود عصام وادي Mahmoud Essam Wadi was martyred after an Israeli drone strike hit him while he was working in central Khan Yunis, in southern Gaza. The attack occurred in an area far from the Yellow Line—the buffer zone established under the ceasefire to separate Israeli-controlled and Palestinian-held areas. According to an CPJ's investigation , Mahmoud had visited their sister’s home in central Khan Younis on Tuesday morning before stepping outside—about 200 meters away—to document the destruction with a drone. At approximately 10:48 a.m., an Israeli drone struck Mahmoud directly as he and fellow freelancer Mohammed Islayeh, 40, were preparing the device for launch. The strike killed Mahmoud and injured Islayeh. His brother, Mohammed Wadi, testified that missile was fired intentionally at Mahmoud, noting that the location was in the middle of Khan Younis and roughly three kilometers from the “yellow line” Israel designated as a no-cross zone. “He was not near Israeli forces nor posing any threat,” he said. “The targeting was deliberate.” He worked independently with several media outlets, including the Qatari-funded broadcaster Al Jazeera and Al Jazeera Mubasher, Al Araby TV, and privately owned Al-Ghad TV. Wadi owned Al-Quds Photography Studio and worked as a freelance photographer. At the time of the strike, he was operating a drone for an Al-Jazeera journalist accompanying him. The drone was launched moments before the attack near the Bani Suhaila roundabout, where he was documenting displacement camps and widespread destruction in what had been designated a “safe” area under the October 2025 ceasefire. Before the war transformed his life, Mahmoud Wadi was a celebrated wedding videographer, renowned for his breathtaking drone shots capturing joy and celebration across Gaza. His studio was destroyed by Israeli airstrikes in April 2025, forcing him to shift from event videography to frontline journalism. Colleagues remembered him as gentle, professional, courageous, and deeply humanitarian. His posts—often tagged #GazaUnderFire—reached thousands, offering raw documentation of the ongoing humanitarian crisis. Reacting to his death, UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese wrote on X: “More grim news from Gaza, the crime scene that never closes. No ceasefire, declared or imagined, can shield Palestinian journalists from Israel’s violence. RIP Mahmoud Wadi. Solidarity to his family, or what remains of it. Between 225 and 250 journalists have been killed in Gaza in just 750 days.” X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: محمد احمد يوسف المنيراوي Killed along with his wife Mirvat Al-Khalidi in an Israeli airstrike on their displacement tent in Al-Saafeen area in the Nuseirat camp, central Gaza. For two years of genocide, Mohammed remained in Gaza City, refusing to leave. However he decided to join the Nuseirat refugee camp to help his family dismantle their tent and return to Gaza City following the ceasefire. At dawn on Wednesday, 29 October 2025, an Israeli strike targeted and killed him Mohammad had captured with his camera footage from the early days of the genocide in Gaza. Alongside his professional work, he pursued his postgraduate studies and earned a master's degree in journalism and media. His professional path was closely intertwined with his human and social values. During the same period, he celebrated his engagement, marriage, and the defense of his master's thesis. Mohammed Al-Minirawi held several important professional positions at Palestine newspaper, including serving as director of its website between 2018 and 2020. He left a clear mark on the platform's development and on strengthening its presence across social media      .

name_en: Ahmad Abu Mutair أحمد أبو مطير
full_name_ar: أحمد أبو مطير Killed in an Israeli violation of the ceasefire by an airstrike on the headquarters of Palestine Media Production Company (PMP) in the Chalets area of Al-Zawayda, central Gaza. The strike destroyed PMP’s rented office, which served as a small production facility providing services to both local and international clients, killing also Ammar al-Zaaneen, the 8 y/o son of company cameraman Mohammed al-Zaaneen, and injuring cameraman Ismail Jabr. Colleagues described him as an exceptionally skilled technician and repairman—some even calling him a “genius”—as well as a highly professional, educated, and open-minded individual. He worked with other PMP journalists in Gaza City from a rented office that included a production facility. In this role, he contributed to providing news and coverage services for both local and international media outlets. PMP also frequently collaborated with the German broadcaster ZDF through its Tel Aviv bureau and correspondents. The Center for the Protection of Palestinian Journalists (PJPC) strongly condemned the crime committed by Israeli Air in flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement that entered into force early last week, which led to the destruction of parts of a large area of the building and severe damage to media equipment. The Israeli Army accused Mutair of being a Hamas platoon commander; an investigation by Der Spiegel found inconsistencies in the document supporting the accusation, and was inconclusive      .

cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Full Name : Muhammad Ismail Al-Kuwaifi | محمد اسماعيل الكويفي Killed in an Israeli strike on a tent on the rooftop of his family's house in Al-Nasr neighborhood in Gaza City. His wife and two children were previously killed on July 3, 2024 in an Israeli strike on his apartment in Al-Tuffah neighborhood eastern Gaza city. He was injured at that time along with his daughter Zeina, who remained with him and became alone after the departure of her father and her family before. He was also known by the nickname Abu Al-Mu’tasim. He studied journalism and earned a master’s degree in management and media leadership. Deeply interested in education, he became a university lecturer and trainer after completing several specialized courses. Professionally, he worked for Al-Aqsa TV and the Shihab and Safa news agencies, producing reports, documentaries, and directing programs and news bulletins, while also collaborating with major international media outlets. Colleagues described him as a dedicated, principled man — passionate about his work, guided by faith, and active both professionally and academically      .

name_en: Mariam Abu Dagga مريم أبو دقة
full_name_ar: مريم رياض أبو فرحانة (أبو دقة) Killed along with 4 other journalists in a double-tap targeted Israeli airstrike on Nasser Medical Complex on the morning of August 25, 2025. Native of Khan Khan Younis, Mariam was an important source of documentation in the southern governorate. Mariam Abu Daqqa's reporting focused on documenting the forced displacement, famine and living conditions. She also documented Israeli massacres in the area. Mariam began her journalism work in 2015 after studying journalism and graduating from Al-Aqsa University in Gaza. Mariam's brother and nephew were killed during the genocide and she had evacuated her only son Ghayth to the UAE while she remained in Gaza to fulfil her journalistic duty. On October 9, 2025, the International Press Institute awarded Abu Dagga the "Hero of World Press Freedom" award, in appreciation of her sacrifices in covering the war in Gaza, denouncing the failure to take measures to hold those involved in her murder accountable. The award statement notes that she "repeatedly risked her life to document the ongoing atrocities in Gaza". The World Press Freedom Champion Award is given annually to journalists who have demonstrated a firm commitment to press freedom and their courage in the face of dangers and challenges      .

cause: Killed by Israel using Tank or Mortar Fire
biography: Killed along with 4 other journalists in a double-tap targeted Israeli airstrike on Nasser Medical Complex on the morning of August 25, 2025. In addition to documenting several Israeli massacres in Khan Younis, Moaz also documented some Israeli violations of the ceasefire in the area. He was also active in documenting forced displacement, living conditions and cases of severely ill children at Nasser Hospital for the purpose of medical evacuations. Less than a week before his murder, Moaz had worked with Haaretz journalists Nir Hasson and Yarden Michaeli who worked on a major article about Israel's engineer famine. Moaz held the camera for the journalists so they can have a virtual tour through a live broadcast from the children's department at Nasser hospital X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: مروة اشرف مسلم Her relatives discovered the fully decomposed bodies of Marwa and her two brothers Moataz and Montaser were found on August 16, 2025. On August 16, 2025, the fully decomposed bodies of journalist Marwa Musallam and her two brothers, Moataz and Montaser, were discovered. The siblings had been pronounced dead on August 1, 2025, after reports emerged of their bodies being found in the Al-Shujaiya neighborhood, eastern Gaza City. However, in a statement published by media outlet Sahat on August 12, Marwa’s close friend, journalist Mariam Al-Dabla, and the Civil Defense spokesperson announced that th house was still inaccessible to Civil Defense crews. Mariam noted that a civilian had managed to reach the location earlier that month and retrieved two decomposed bodies, which were not yet identified at the time. The absence of a third body led to uncertainty about Marwa and her brothers' exact whereabouts. Contact with Marwa and her brothers was lost on July 5, 2025, following an Israeli airstrike that targeted a house adjacent to theirs in Al-Shaaf area, eastern Gaza City. The siblings were presumed dead until July 28, 2025 when one of her brothers living in Russia confirmed receiving a call from Marwa's phone number. In response, the Palestinian Journalists Syndicate organized a vigil on July 29, 2025, outside the Solidarity Media Center in Gaza City, calling for her rescue. The syndicate also appealed to UNOCHA and the Red Cross, which responded by saying that the IDF was delaying its response, while other international NGOs stated they only evacuate living individuals. Marwa Musallam worked for the local Al-Shabab ("youth") radio station hosting the daily morning program and other programs addressing the living conditions in Gaza      .

full_name_ar: أنس جمال محمود الشريف Killed in an Israeli assassination airstrike targeting him in his Al Jazeera press tent. The airstrike killed 6 people including 5 Al Jazeera staff, and journalist Muhammad Al-Khalidi. The IDF and Israeli media had repeatedly incited against Anas Al-Sharif since as early as March 2024 accusing him without substance of being affiliated with Hamas. Anas was hired by Al Jazeera early in the genocide following their discovery of his visual documentation of Israeli strikes on his hometown of Jabalia, North Gaza. He was assigned within a few weeks to officially become a correspondent. The IDF had bombed his family home in late 2023 killing his father. Despite multiple ground invasions of North Gaza, Anas remained there until his colleagues were chased and shot by Israeli drones in October 2024. He then moved to report from Al-Ahli hospital. After Israel bombed Al-Ahli hospital on April 13, 2024, Anas moved to report from Al-Shifa hospital where he was killed. He was reporting day and night from thse fixed workplace clearly known to the public and to the IDF, contrary to the latter's claim of him being a "cell leader". Anas was dubbed "The voice of Gaza" by the locals and had built world renown through his footage and live reports, numbering in the hundreds, Anas was instrumental in documenting Israeli war crimes in all their forms across northern Gaza from bombings of homes, schools, hospitals, displacement, starvation, assassinations of his close colleagues and other aspects of living conditions. Anas studied journalism at the Media faculty of Al-Aqsa University in Gaza. He was encouraged to pursue journalism by his mentor journalist Imad Zaqout who saw potential in him      .

full_name_ar: ولاء الجعبري
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Killed while pregnant along with her husband Dr. Amjad Al-Shaer—medical director of Al-Shifa Hospital— and their children Hasan, Izz-ed-Din, Mira, and Amir, in an Israeli airstrike on their apartment in Tal al-Hawa, Gaza City. Walaa's fetus was ejected from the womb. Walaa started her career at Al-Risala newspaper, then moving to the government-run Al-Rai Radio, before joining the Media Department at the Ministry of Justice. name_en: Ahmad Abu Isha أحمد أبو عيشة
full_name_ar: أحمد سلامه هاشم ابوعيشة Killed in an Israeli airstrike while he was at his home's doorstep in Al-Sawarha area in Al-Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza. At around 16:50 on 10 July 2025, an Israeli drone targeted journalist Ahmed Salama Hashim Abu ‘Aisha (34), who held a PHD and worked for Palestine Today News Agency, with a missile while he was in the garden of his house located in al-Sawarah area, southwest of al-Nusirat refugee camp. As a result, Ahmed sustained shrapnel injuries in his back and lower limbs. He was transported to al-‘Awda Hospital in al-Nusirat camp, where he was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) but succumbed to his injuries less than an hour later. Ahmed’s brother, Mahmoud Salama Hashim Abu ‘Aisha (38), said to PCHR’s researcher: “I was standing on the street, specifically in front of the house gate, while my brother Ahmed (34), a journalist holding a PhD in literature and criticism, was sitting on a bed in the garden and reading the Quran. Suddenly, a loud explosion occurred, filling the area with dust and smoke. I rushed inside and found my brother Ahmed lying on the ground and severely bleeding. Ahmed was directly targeted with a drone missile, injuring him in his back and lower limbs. He was still breathing, so I immediately carried him, fearing he would be targeted again, and placed him on a motorcycle (tuk-tuk). I rushed him to al-‘Awda Hospital in al-Nusirat refugee camp. Due to the severity of his condition, he was admitted to the ICU, and at around 17:40 on the same day, he was pronounced dead, succumbing to his injuries."      .

full_name_ar: محمود أكرم أحمد الحناوي Mahmoud Akram Al-Hanawi was a 31-year-old freelance photojournalist and media worker from Gaza. He tragically lost his life on July 6, 2025, after an Israeli warplane bombed the home he had taken refuge in within Gaza City. According to Gaza Notifications, the Israeli airstrike killed Ahmad Akram Al-Hanawi and his two daughters, Mayar and Alma, in a missile strike that targeted Gaza City." In detail, his colleague, journalist Sally Thabet, told a “SKYz” correspondent: “An Israeli warplane targeted the house where my colleague Mahmoud had taken refuge, which led to his martyrdom along with several displaced people who were inside the house.” X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

name_en: Muhammad Imad Al-Sultan محمد عماد السلطان
full_name_ar: محمد عماد محمد السلطان Killed in an Israeli airstrike on his family home, along with his father-in-law and director of the Indonesian hospital Dr. Marwan Al-Sultan, and the latter's wife and five offspring. Journalist Mohammed al-Sultan, an editor and language reviewer for the Palestine daily newspaper in Gaza, was arrested by Israeli forces on September 24, 2023, after seeking refuge in a school following the destruction of his home. He was detained for 15 months, including in the Sde Teiman Israeli torture camp. During his detention, he was subjected to eight harsh interrogation sessions, physical violence, and degrading treatment. He was held for more than 17 months and was released on February 28, 2025, as part of a prisoner exchange between Israel and Hamas      .

cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Killed in an Israeli airstrike on Al-Baqa cafe on the seashore in Gaza City, along with 33 other individuals. Journalist Bayan Abu Sultan was also wounded in the airstrike. Ismail Abu Hatab had worked as a photojournalist with several media outlets. He was scheduled to lead a digital security training workshop for local journalists during the same week he was killed. According to the PJPC, Ismail was seriously injured in November 2024 while documenting the bombing of Burj Al-Ghafri. The Al-Baqa cafe where he was killed was the centerpiece of his Los Angeles photography exhibition, "Between Sky and Sea," portraying life under siege and bombardment. Ismail had described the exhibition, saying: “In every image there is a soul, in every voice inside the tent there is a memory, and in every detail there is the pulse of Gaza"      .

full_name_ar: أحمد قلجة
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Killed after succumbing to wounds sustained in an Israeli drone airstrike that targeted him and a group of journalists in the courtyard of Al-Ahli Arab (Baptist) Hospital in Gaza City. On the spot, the Israeli strike had initially killed 3 journalists and wounded two others, including Ahmad Qalaja. Three other journalists were injured in the attack: Emad Daloul, a correspondent for Palestine Today TV, and brothers Islam and Imam Badr, who were reporting and filming for Al-Araby TV. Witnesses said the group had been working on their laptops in the courtyard when the missile struck. Video footage reviewed by CPJ confirmed Qalaja was hit while seated in his work area. Qalaja had recently graduated in journalism and media from Al-Azhar University in Gaza and had begun working as a cameraman at the start of the war. His father, himself a media professional, said he had encouraged his son’s passion for journalism. The Israel Defense Forces stated the strike was a “precise” attack on an Islamic Jihad operative operating from a command center in the hospital courtyard. IDF spokesperson Avichay Adraee later claimed that Hajjaj and Al-Rifai were Islamic Jihad members “masquerading as journalists,” but provided no evidence. Palestine Today TV condemned the attack as a “double war crime,” arguing that it involved the direct targeting of both journalists and a hospital, which are protected under international law. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) sought further comment from the IDF but received no response      .

biography: Killed along with two other journalists in an Israeli strike on a group of journalists in the courtyard of Al-Ahli hospital. The strike killed Baddah and Hajjaj and gravely wounded Qalaja, who died from his injuries one day later on June 6. Palestine Today TV correspondent Emad Daloul was also injured, as were two other journalists with Al-Araby TV: reporter Islam Badr and camera operator Imam Badr. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) stated they targeted an Islamic Jihad operative in the yard of Al-Ahli Hospital. IDF spokesperson Avichay Adraee later claimed that Suleiman Hajjaj and Samir Al-Rifai, both killed in the strike, were Islamic Jihad members posing as journalists and using the hospital to support militant activity. No evidence was provided to support these accusations. In a statement, Palestine Today TV mourned the deaths of its journalists Suleiman Hajjaj and Ismail Badah. The channel condemned the strike as a "double war crime"—for targeting both journalists and a civilian hospital, both protected under international law. It accused Israel of conducting a systematic campaign to silence the media and hide alleged war crimes, enabled by international silence and complicity, particularly the U.S. veto of a UN Security Council ceasefire resolution. The channel reaffirmed its commitment to continuing its journalistic mission despite the risks and loss, and called on international organizations to take real action to protect journalists X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: يوسف حماد النخالة Killed on the evening of Saturday, May 31? 2025, when an Israeli airstrike targeted his home in Al-Nafaq area of Gaza City. According to Al-Jazeera journalist Mohammed Qraiqea, Yousef's home was bombed without warning around 6 PM and was completely destroyed. His body remained trapped under the debris, as civil defense rescue teams were unable to retrieve it due to the extensive destruction and their limited resources. He was killed after a long and exhausting workday. He had been on duty at the National Media Company, which provides broadcast services to Al Jazeera and other news outlets during live coverage. He was responsible for directing live transmissions, managing satellite uplinks and frequencies, and had been continuing the work of former engineer Rami Al-Rifi, who himself was killed along with Ismaïl Al-Ghoul in an targeted airstrike on their car on July 31, 2024      .

full_name_ar: معتز محمد رجب Killed in an Israeli airstrike on a vehicle on Al-Nafaq Street in Gaza City along with three civilians. Mu'ataz Rajab (24 years old), was a cameraman and editor for Al-Quds TV, was killed in a targeted airstrike in Gaza City on Wednesday evening. According to the testimony of Loay Rajab, a family member to the MADA Center, an Israeli reconnaissance drone fired at least one missile at a civilian vehicle traveling on Al-Nafaq Street in Gaza City at around 7:00PM. The strike directly hit journalist, killing him instantly along with three other civilians. He was on a journalistic assignment at the time, engaged in media coverage      .

name_en: Hassaan Abu Warda حسان أبو وردة
full_name_ar: حسان مجدي أبو وردة Founder of Barq Gaza (برق غزة) news agency & Director of Barq News Agency. Killed along with a number of relatives in an Israeli airstrike on his family in Jabalia al-Nazla in North Gaza, at dawn on Sunday. According to the testimony of his brother Mohammed, to the MADA Center, he was sleeping with his family inside their home in Jabalia Al-Nazla at around 1:00AM on Sunday, when Israeli F16 warplanes bombed the house with a missile that caused it to collapse on the residents. The strike occurred without prior warning and was sudden, resulting in the deaths of most of those inside, including his brother Hassan, their parents, and their younger brother. The bodies were recovered with difficulty from under the rubble and debris. Some had turned into fragments, including his brother Hassan. They were transported by ambulance to hospitals in Gaza City      .

The director of the “Noor Media Network”, journalist Mohammad Amin Abu Daqqa (42 years old), was killed after being targeted by a missile fired from a drone while he was displaced and walking along the main street in the town of Abasan Al-Kabira at around 11:00AM on Tuesday morning. full_name_ar: نور قنديل
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Killed along with her husband, journalist Khaled Abu Sayf, and their daughter in an Israeli strike on their home in Deir al-Balah. According to Al Manassa, journalist Nour Qandil, her husband, fellow journalist Khaled Abu Youssef, and their young daughter (1 y/o) were killed when an Israeli missile struck a neighbor's home in western Deir al-Balah in central Gaza. The explosion destroyed several nearby houses, wiping out the family. Before the war, Nour was active in youth-led media initiatives and was deeply committed to supporting young journalists and promoting local storytelling. On May 15, Palestinian journalist Nour Qandil wrote a Facebook post saying, “If I am martyred, I am not just a number, right? Tell me a lot about me, and let my voice, my ambition, and my dream be heard after me.” She dreamed of traveling to complete her master's degree in digital media, but she remained trapped by the blockade imposed on Gaza for more than two decades. Nour Qandil was a 2020 graduate of the Department of Journalism and Media at Al-Aqsa University, has not had stable employment opportunities in local media outlets. However, she has worked with several organizations, most recently with Al-Thuraya Media, where she served as an events coordinator at the Social Media Café. Her colleagues described her as “talented, resilient, and persistent,” and she always sought to break the economic blockade by developing her handicraft skills and marketing them through social media platforms. “Nour had an extraordinary passion for journalism… Even after she had a child, she didn’t give up on her dream. She wanted to convey the voice of Gaza, especially the stories of women and families.”Nour wasn't looking for stardom, but for a voice. At the moment of truth, when the horizon narrowed and the bombing intensified, she wrote: "Tell me a lot, and convey my voice and ambition..." Her family was displaced several times during the war, and in mid-May, they returned to their home in Deir al-Balah, believing that calm might return. But three days later, Israeli warplanes directly bombed the house      .

full_name_ar: عبد الرحمن توفيق العبادلة Killed in an Israeli airstrike on the town of Al-Qarara, east of Khan Yunis. He was confirmed killed on May 18 after contact with him was lost two days prior. The photojournalist at “Al-Nahar News Agency,” ABDEL RAHMAN TAWFIQ AL-ABADLEH (35 years old), was killed as a result of a bombing that targeted his home in the town of Al-Qarara, east of Khan Younis. His body was found on Monday morning, a day after he went missing. According to the testimony of Amer Al-Farra, a neighbor of the martyred journalist , he had gone on the evening of Sunday, May 18, 2025, to the Al-Qarara area east of Khan Younis to check on his home and retrieve some belongings after being displaced due to the new Israeli evacuation orders for residents in the area. When he did not return, his family became concerned—especially since his mobile phone was switched off, which increased their worry. At around 7:00AM the following morning, some of his family members went out to search for him and check on his condition. They found him lying in a pool of blood, having been killed by an Israeli drone missile strike near his home. His body was recovered with difficulty due to the ongoing drone presence in the area and was transferred to Nasser Medical Complex      .

full_name_ar: حسن عبد الفتاح محمد اصليح Killed in a targeted Israeli airstrike on him while he was recovering from an injury at Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis. Hassan was injured in the journalists' massacre on April 7, 2025, when an Israeli airstrike directly struck press tents around the same hospital, killing two journalists and injuring several others. He was the target of that airstrike as officially announced by IDF spokespeople on X. Although he had survived, he sustained injuries to the head and had lost two fingers in the aftermath. Hassan Eslayeh was a crucial source of documentation of Israeli war crimes, massacres, aftermaths of ground invasions, forced displacement, and living conditions in Khan Younis throughout the genocide. Moreover, he consistently helped desperate Palestinian families share appeals for help, particularly those suffering from life-threatening health conditions and needing urgent medical treatment. Israel had killed 7 of Hassan's relatives on the night of March 18, 2025, when it broke the ceasefire. His family home was also completely destroyed by Israeli strikes. On September 5, 2024, prominent Israeli media accounts on social media launched an incitement campaign to murder Hassan because he "documented the abduction of soldiers and bodies" on October 7, 2023. Hassan Eslayeh was regarded as highly trusted veteran journalist and a mentor to young journalists in Gaza; He had also provided financial assistance to the families of fellow journalists killed in the same assassination attempt that injured him. The Gaza Media Office called the attack a “double crime” — targeting both a journalist and a patient in a hospital. The Palestinian Ministry of Health condemned the strike as a heinous violation of international law, accusing Israel of systematically dismantling the healthcare system      .

full_name_ar: نور الدين عبدو
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Full name : Noor al-Din Matar Abdu | نور الدين مطر عبدو • Reporter for Al-Rai Radio. Field correspondent for Al-Sharq News Agency • Killed in an Israeli bombardment of Al-Karama School in the Al-Tuffah neighborhood in eastern Gaza City while wearing a clearly marked press vest. • Local sources reported that Israeli warplanes targeted him in a second airstrike directly after he arrived to the school to document the aftermath of the first strike. • Human rights activist and head of EuroMed Hman Rights Monitor Ramy Abdu announced the death of his relative on X: "Just moments ago, my beloved cousin, journalist Nour Al-Din Matar Abdu, was killed by an Israeli missile while carrying out his journalistic duties." • He lost his brother, journalist Mohammed Abdo, in 2007 during previous conflict. He continued his work out of commitment to truth and documenting suffering, refusing to evacuate northern Gaza despite personal risk and home destruction. He was actively involved in humanitarian efforts — distributing aid and helping children in displacement camps. • His last words to his family: “I feel like I’m living my last hours.” His last prayer: “O God, if you have chosen me, make me whole, not in pieces.” • His camera survived the blast and remained as a witness      .

full_name_ar: فاطمة حسونة
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Full name of the martyr : Fatima Raed Muhammad Hassouna | فاطمه رائد محمد حسونه • Killed along with relatives, including her five siblings, in a night Israeli airstrike on her family home in eastern Gaza City. • Hassona contributed to several news outlets, including the local platform Untold Palestine, the U.S.-based outlet Mondoweiss, and as an anonymous contributor to The Guardian. • Fatima's murder came just a day after the announcement that a documentary in which she is featured was selected for the 2025 Cannes Film Festival. • According to Middle East Eye : Fatma Hassouna described her work as a kind of resistance against Israel's war, loading her camera with memory cards as if placing bullets in a gun. Her camera, she said in a recent interview, was her rifle. "It changes the world and defends me... I can document people's stories, so that my family's stories too don't just vanish into thin air," (...) "It's not really about whether the world sees it. What matters to me is what I'm doing and how lasting the impact of my work will be. Will this work live forever? I strive for my photos to be everlasting." • From the Palestinian Journalist Protection Center: Fatima’s powerful photos documenting life under siege were published globally, shedding light on the human toll of the war. Her killing raises the journalist death toll in Gaza to 212 since October 7—an unprecedented number in modern conflict history. • From the Yura Collective: Fatma Hassouna, a photographer from Gaza, graduated in Multimedia from the University College of Applied Sciences. She has worked as a photographer with the Tamer Foundation for Community Education and as a member of the editorial team for the literary group "Yara'at Al Adabi." Additionally, she has worked as a photographer with the Women's Affairs Foundation and as a member of the "She Leads" program with the organization Plan International. Her works have been showcased in several local exhibitions. • According to France 24: A multimedia graduate of the Gaza University College of Applied Sciences, Fatma Hassouna posted her photos on her Instagram account, which was followed by 35,000 people. At the same time, she led writing workshops for children at a school in northern Gaza. The newly married young woman had just been the subject of a documentary by Iranian director Sepideh Farsi entitled "Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk," in which she played the lead role. The film was to be screened a few hours later at the Cannes Film Festival , in the "ACID" (Association of Independent Cinema for its Distribution) selection. • Plan International statement on Fatima Hassouneh on 17th April 2025 "A talented photographer and former participant in Plan International’s She Leads programme, for the last 18 months Fatima has bravely shared multiple accounts of daily life in Gaza with her work published in the Guardian and other media outlets." (...)“Fatima has been a beacon of inspiration for all of us at Plan International,” said Dr Unni Krishnan, Global Humanitarian Director. “Through her fearless storytelling and unwavering courage in the face of conflict, she gave the world a window into the human cost of war—and into the heart of Gaza. We came to know Fatima not just as a powerful voice, but as a person full of love—for life, for art, and above all, for the people of Gaza. Her legacy will stay with us forever." X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

biography: Full name : Ahmed Rouhi Mansour | احمد روحي منصور • Palestine Today new agency editor and Correspondent and for Palestine Today TV • Killed in an Israeli airstrike that directly targeted press tents next to the Nasser Medical Complex compound in Khan Younis at 2:45 am. His colleague Hilmi Al-Faqaawi died on the spot whereas Ahmad Mansour had suffered severe burns as was seen in footage showing being burned alive while being unable to move from his desk. Ahmad Mansour succumbed to his injuries around 2:30 am the next day. Another civilian accompanying the crew was killed by shrapnel in his sleep that killed him on the spot. Seven other prominent journalists were also injured. • According to Palestinian media outlets, the tent that was targeted belonged to Palestine Today TV      .

full_name_ar: إسلام نصر الدين مقداد • She was a freelance journalist • Killed along with her son Adam in an Israeli airstrike on the Abdulhadi family's house in Al-Amal neighborhood west of Khan Younis. I am not just a number.” X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: يوسف حسونة
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: • Photojournalist who worked notably with Agence France Presse (AFP). He also contributed to and wrote articles about Gaza for several media outlets including Libération, Le Devoir and Al-Monitor. • Killed in the Israeli bombing of the Dar al-Arqam school turned shelter • Hassouna has worked with AFP since 2014 and remains in Gaza, having been displaced ten times. Since the start of the war, Hassouna has been one of AFP's most prominent freelance video reporters in the Strip. • Yousef Hassouna was awarded the prestigious Rory Peck award for his live extensive coverage of events in Gaza post October 7 with the photojournalist Bilal Sabbagh. Both worked for Agence France-Presse in Gaza. “Bilal and Youssef’s work is remarkable for its different emotions. We understand the horrific scale of the devastation thanks to their drone images,” the jury said, describing them as “unforgettable scenes.” AFP news director Phil Chetonde said, “Everyone at AFP is incredibly proud of Bilal and his colleagues’ work in Gaza. This award is a well-deserved reward for his excellent journalism in almost impossible conditions.” X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: محمد عماد منصور • Correspondent for Palestine Today TV and a Japanese newspaper named Asahi Shimbun (it means "morning sun newspaper") • Killed in Israeli airstrikes that targeted the apartment he was renting in southern Khan Younis. According to his colleague at Palestine Today Ibrahim Ibrahim and witnesses, the apartment was struck with at least 3 missiles. Mohammad had headed back to his place in the Batn al-Sameen area to rest when Israeli drones launched 2 projectiles at his room at 0:55 am, then struck him again as he, wounded, tried to leave the apartment. He sustained shrapnel to his abdomen, severing a main artery. • Mohammad's wife is critically injured and suffered brain hemorrhage. • The IDF had launched a series of airstrikes across southern Gaza starting around 1:30 which led to the murder of at least 23 people. • Mohammad Mansour was one of the key reporters on events unfolding in southern Gaza      .

full_name_ar: حسام باسل شبات • Reporter for Al Jazeera Mubasher and contributor to Drop Site News. He was also deeply involved in organizing, promoting and actively contributing to charitable initiatives to alleviate the suffering of displaced families      .

cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: • Journalist for ABC News : he was a sound engineer for ABC News for 20 years until 2014, when he left the company and became a teacher. He lived in Gaza City with his wife, daughter and three sons, but he was in Deir al Balah in a displacement camp when he was killed. • Killed along with his wife and daughter in an Israeli airstrike on their home in Gaza City while they were asleep. name_en: Mahmoud Isleem Al-Basos محمود اسليم البسوس
full_name_ar: محمود سمير اسليم البسوس (In the Forbidden stories article, he is called Mahmoud Isleem Al-Basos, and he is referenced in https://www.shireen.ps/ as Mahmoud Samir Misbah Al-Basos, 25y/o | محمود سمير مصباح البسوس ) • Bassous started collaborating with Shadi Al-Tabatibi on Drone and photography journalism. Tabatibi began assigning him photography tasks, and Bassous also started working with international media like Reuters and Anadolu Agency. • Killed in two successive airstrikes against a crew of journalists and 8 aid workers affiliated with the UK-based Al-Khair Foundation who were documenting relief efforts led by this charitable Foundation in Beit Lahia. • In early March, during the ceasefire, Forbidden Stories asked Mahmoud Samir Isleem Al-Basos to film Gaza. The idea was to continue the work of journalists killed or injured during the war while enabling readers to visualize the unprecedented scale of destruction through detailed 3D maps. • That morning, two Israeli air strikes killed at least seven other people. Among them were aid workers and cameramen dispatched by Al-Khair. The NGO explained that it was using a drone to film the preparation of a Ramadan meal and the future extension of a refugee camp. • According to his cousin, quoted by the CPJ, he was wearing his press vest and helmet. • The Israeli army claimed that these strikes were aimed at “terrorists”—two of whom were operating a drone—and issued an error-filled list of names and photos. Mahmoud Samir Isleem Al-Basos is neither mentioned nor pictured in the list of “terrorists.” Instead, (Investigation led by Forbidden stories (gathered 15 international medias) found a name that resembles his, belonging to an individual described by the Israeli army as “a Hamas terrorist operating under journalistic cover.” Based on their research, the individual named by the army has no direct link with Al-Basos and was not killed in the strike. The military also denounced a connection between the drone used in Beit Lahia and the Palestinian Islamic Jihad without providing any evidence. • According to the journalists who knew him, as well as the Al-Khair Foundation and a Hamas representative we interviewed, Al-Basos had no affiliation with Hamas or the Palestinian Islamic Jihad. • Bellingcat have also geolocated the two strikes in Beit Lahia: the first around two kilometers from the Israeli border and an Israeli army post and the second around three kilometers away. D drone at this distance doesn't represent a threat to the Israeli army, as it claims. When asked on two separate occasions to provide evidence supporting its accusations, the Israeli military stated that it would “not elaborate on the published statements.” More generally, they said it “categorically reject[ed] the allegation of a systemic attack on journalists.” • “Israel has repeatedly made similar unproven claims without producing any credible evidence,” explained Doja Daoud from the CPJ. “We know that this practice endangers journalists and erodes public trust in Palestinian journalists reporting from Gaza.” The CPJ has just added Al-Basos to its list of journalists killed by the Israeli army and refers to his case as “murder.” __ Picture by courtesy of Shadi Al-Tabatibi X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

biography: Full name : Ahmed Hisham Zahdi Abu Al-Rous | أحمد هشام زهدي ابو الروس • Killed in an Israeli drone strike on his car in the Nuseirat camp, central Gaza along with five people on January 15, 2025, days before a ceasefire between Israel and Gaza began. • He worked as a reporter and photographer for the local Assulta Arrabaa (Fourth Estate) news agency. • Ahmad was active in social projects. • His father, Hisham Abu Al-Rous, told CPJ that: “At around 5 p.m. on Wednesday, a few days before the truce went into effect, Ahmed was driving his car with his twin brother Mohammed and three friends in the Nuseirat refugee camp. Of course, they did not pose any threat to the Israeli occupation, so an Israeli drone fired a single missile at them, killing all five.” • Fourth Estate’s editor-in-chief, Youssef Rayyan, told CPJ: “Ahmed worked with us at the agency from June 1, 2023, until his martyrdom, and he was providing the agency with news and photos while he was recently at the Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in the city of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza.” • Abu Al-Rous was buried in the Nuseirat camp on January 16, 2025      .

full_name_ar: أحمد الشياح
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Killed in an Israeli airstrike targeting a food distribution point (a soup kitchen) in the so-called "humanitarian zone" in Mawasi Khan Younis, in the southern Gaza Strip. According to his brother, Mohammed, his family’s displacement tent was near the food distribution area but they didn’t expect the bombs would be aimed at the area “since it is a known place and provides humanitarian services to the displaced.”. Ahmed Al-Shayah, a Palestinian freelance journalist specializing in producing documentary films and television programs in Gaza, was also Broadcast Reporter, Editor, Internet Reporter & Producer. He contributed to Al Jazeera and Quds Press Agency. As investigative action, the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) reached out to the Israel Defense Forces’ North America Media Desk to ask whether they were aware that civilians and journalists were present in the area they bombed, and whether Al Shayyah was targeted for his journalistic work. As usual, CPJ did not receive a response at the time of reporting. CPJ chose thus the "dangerous assignment" cause of death, even if CPJ noted that Mohammed Al Shayyah said his brother, Ahmed, was in a food distribution area “in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis, the Israeli warplanes directly targeted it, which resulted in his direct martyrdom." X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: أحلام نافذ التلولي • Photojournalist and anchor at Tahreer Press channel, as well as a correspondent for Drop Site News and B'Tselem to whom she contributed by documenting the situation in North Gaza. • Killed in evening Israeli "firebelt" airstrikes on residential buildings around Al-Ghifari intersection on Al-Jalaa Street in Gaza City. She was looking for a place to access internet when a nearby house was bombed. • The IDF had launched at least 15 airstrikes across all areas of the Gaza (City) governorate on January 13, killing around 60 people in the governorate alone. Another journalist, Muhammad Al-Talmas, was also killed in those airstrikes. • Drop Site paid tribute to her as "a trusted source, providing detailed reporting, video, and information to Drop Site News and others, chronicling through her words and images the genocide in northern Gaza and capturing evidence of Israeli war crimes from the besieged Indonesian Hospital." • Ahlam's wheelchair-bound elderly father was shot and killed by Israeli snipers mid-December 2023 as residents of North Gaza were being forcibly displaced. Her sister Maryam was also killed by snipers on May 15, 2024. She left their school-shelter holding a white flag to rescue a young man who was shot and injured by snipers. She was shot with 4-5 bullets according to Ahlam who witnessed the murder      .

full_name_ar: عمر صلاح صالح الديراوي • Freelance photojournalist working for the Martyrs of Al-Aqsa Hospital. • Killed along with his parents and brother in an Israeli airstrike on his family’s home in Zawayda, central Gaza. full_name_ar: اريج علي ابراهيم شاهين Photojournalist, she posted photos and news updates about the war in Gaza on her Instagram page, which had more than 13,000 followers, covering all the shelling near her home in the Nuseirat camp, and documenting the genocide at the Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah and the Al-Awda Hospital in the Nuseirat camp in central Gaza. Killed along with her mother in an Israeli airstrike on their home in Nuseirat, central Gaza. According to her brother, Ayman Shaheen, Areej studied accounting but loved photography and began to take classes to specialize in covering weddings and happy gatherings.“But during the war the parties stopped and based on the fact that photography is also a message, she began documenting the crimes of the Israeli occupation in central Gaza through video and photography,". Gaza Martyr published her sister testimony on X: “A passionate wedding photographer, she was about to deliver a groom’s photos at the last minute when she was targeted, and she was also supposed to photograph a wedding in Khan Younis the next day, but fate had decided otherwise. She had won a photography competition in Belgium on the children of Gaza.” X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: حسن سعيد حلمي القيشاوي Palestinian journalist Hassan al-Qishawi was killed following an Israeli drone strike that targeted him in west of Gaza City while documenting the aftermath of an Israeli airstrike. According to his brother,Hashem Al-Qishawi, he began filming the airstrike’s impact on his cellphone because he did not have his camera with him: “About half an hour later, another drone fired a missile at him, killing him instantly.” Hassan Al-Qishawi was a freelance photographer who worked for the Indonesian news site Gaza Media and its affiliated humanitarian organization INH. Muhammad Husein Gaza, founder of INH and Gazamedia, said Hasan Qisyawi was part of Gazamedia's initial team which was founded in 2018. Thanks to his dedication, Hasan was recruited to the INH media team since 2010: “Since October 7, Hasan has been the spearhead of the INH institution in the process of distributing humanitarian aid from the Indonesian people through INH which operates in the northern region until today he was martyred,” said Husein in his statement      .

full_name_ar: فادي حسونة
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Video editor at Al-Quds Today TV. Fadi Hassouna began his journalistic career early, working for Al-Quds Al-Youm TV since 2020, despite being a student at Al-Isra University majoring in web design and development. His skills have made him a key player in covering Israeli attacks on Gaza. As the war intensified, so did his sense of mission. Every day, Fadi worked from a broadcast van parked in front of Al-Awda Hospital in Nuseirat camp, documenting the unfolding destruction. His father, Ihab Hassouna, recalled seeing him only “three days a month.” Fadi believed that journalism was a duty — to show the world what his people were enduring. His family, worried for his safety, urged him to marry during their displacement. But Fadi refused, saying he would not marry until he returned to Gaza. His heart remained in his city, and in his work — a camera in his hand, purpose in his eyes. On December 26, 2024, Fadi and four colleagues were killed when an Israeli missile struck the van of the channel's press car which was parked in front of Al-Awda Al-Nusseirat Hospital in Nuseirat camp, central Gaza. The strike set the vehicle on fire killing 5 members of Al-Quds Today TV's staff. The fire consumed their bodies; Fadi was only identified by his heel and small stature. Yet those who knew Fadi say his courage will not be forgotten. “Fadi was an example of determination,” said his friend Mohammed Abu Odeh. “He believed the truth must reach the world — and we’ll carry that message forward, even if it costs us our lives.” X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: محمد الشُرافي
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: The freelance journalist Mohammad Al-Sharafi was killed in an Israeli airstrike on the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza. Mohammed Al-Sharafi, a 25-year-old Palestinian journalist and freelance photographer for Al-Aqsa TV, was killed along with his brothers Moaz and Diaa in an Israeli strike on the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza. Their bodies were found by neighbors two days later. The family had been forced to flee Jabalia to Gaza City during the Israeli military operation, but the three brothers were unable to evacuate and remained in the camp. A correspondent for Al-Aqsa TV confirmed that Mohammed had been working as a freelance photographer and editor since June and had stayed behind when other journalists evacuated      .

full_name_ar: ميسرة أحمد صلاح • Journalist at the editing and design department at Quds News Network • He succumbed to injuries sustained from Israeli raid in North Gaza. Specifically, he sustained serious injuries to the head and abdomen a few days prior to his death when the IDF raided and attacked the Awni Al-Harthani School in Beit Lahia, The last Israeli raid on the school occurred on the evening of November 27, 2024. • Maysara was taken to the barely functioning Kamal Adwan Hospital and his condition required a transfer to either Al-Ahli or Al-Shifa hospitals. On November 30, Israeli forces held the ambulance transporting him for eight hours at the checkpoint separating North Gaza and Gaza City, His condition consequently deteriorated and he died inside the ambulance before reaching the hospital. • Quds published a statement on X, on December 1, 2024: "Obituary. With profound sorrow and grief, Quds News Network mourns its colleague, journalist Maysara Salah, who was martyred after succumbing to injuries sustained from Israeli occupation forces' gunfire in the northern Gaza Strip. Our colleague Maysara was targeted during the Gaza war, in which the occupation continues to destroy everything in its path and kill people in every way imaginable. Our colleague was wounded near the Awani al-Harthani School in the northern Gaza Strip, following a heavy Israeli bombardment that targeted the school, which was sheltering hundreds of displaced people. These people have been trapped under conditions of starvation and insecurity for over two months due to the ongoing military aggression. Despite the tireless efforts of the medical staff at Kamal Adwan Hospital to save his life, the occupation refused to allow his transfer to hospitals in Gaza City for necessary treatment on Saturday, November 30, 2024. After strenuous attempts to transfer him to the Arab National Hospital (Baptist Hospital) or al-Shifa Hospital, the occupation forces obstructed the ambulance and detained our colleague Maysara for eight consecutive hours. He was finally allowed to pass after he had passed away due to the delay in receiving treatment Quds News Network holds the Israeli occupation fully responsible for the martyrdom of our colleague Maysara Salah, who was killed twice: once by direct injury, and again by obstructing his access to necessary medical treatment. The network calls on human rights and international organizations to open an immediate and comprehensive investigation into the ongoing war crimes committed by the occupation against Palestinian journalists, which have so far resulted in the martyrdom of more than 190 journalists, in flagrant violation of all international laws and norms. To God we belong and to Him we shall return. Sunday, December 1, 2024" X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: محمد صالح الشريف Palestinian journalist killed by an Israeli drone that shot him dead in the vicinity of Kamal Adwan Hospital. After several days, he returned with his cousin to check on his home when the drone opened fire on them. Mohammad's cousin was killed first, then he bled to death for more than two hours. Israeli forces killed a Palestinian journalist in a drone attack on north Gaza on Saturday, the Wafa news agency reported, citing local sources      .

biography: Haneen Mahmoud Baroud, working for Al-Quds Foundation was killed on the airstrike on Asma School, which houses displaced people in Al-Shati refugee camp. full_name_ar: سائد رضوان
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Saed Radwan, a Palestinian journalist and manager of the digital media department of the Hamas-owned Al-Aqsa TV, was killed alongside eight others in an Israeli airstrike on a school sheltering displaced Palestinian families in Shati camp in Gaza City on October 27, 2024. The airstrike also killed freelance journalists Haneen Baroud and Nadia Emad Al Sayed. Emad Al Sayed’s husband, Muhammad Masoud, told CPJ they were surprised when Israel began bombing the school around 1:15 p.m., including one of the classrooms they turned into a make-shift newsroom. The head of the programs department at Al-Aqsa Radio, Ahmed Zughbour, told CPJ that “the strike was direct to the classroom they were in. to the point that our colleague Saed was shattered into pieces, and our colleague Nadia was also difficult to recognize at first.” CPJ emailed the IDF’s North America Desk inquiring whether it knew that civilians and journalists were in the school when Israeli forces bombed it. On October 29 the IDF reiterated its claim to CPJ that it "directs its strikes only towards military targets" and asserted that "many" are members of Hamas military and "were therefore lawful targets," but provided no evidence to substantiate its claimsRole: Head of Digital Media Department at Al-Aqsa TV 3 journalists among the martyrs of the Asmaa School massacre, which was bombed by the occupation in Al-Shati camp, west of Gaza City Journalist Wael Abo Omer writes: "Fellow journalist Saed Radwan Abu Osama was a walking Quran. Gentleman, good-natured, with a good reputation and distinguished dealings in all aspects of his life We found him smiling in the darkest and most difficult circumstances. May God have mercy on you and accept you, martyr of the homeland." full_name_ar: علي نسمان
cause: Killed by Israel using an Airstrike
biography: Ali Abdullah Hassan Al-Nisman (April 15, 1985 – October 13, 2023) is a Palestinian political activist, comedian and blogger who was killed during an Israeli raid on the Gaza Strip on Friday.. He participated in several Palestinian series, including The Soul , The Heaven's Gate and The Fedayeen . He was active on social media as a Palestinian blogger and was one of the most prominent bloggers. He was active against the Israeli occupation and the Oslo Accords led by the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank . He was one of the most prominent activists during Operation Flood of Al-Aqsa . Al-Nisman was born in Gaza on April 15, 1985. He hails from the northern Gaza City and spent most of his life there. He finished high school and then obtained a bachelor’s degree in business and finance management and a diploma in organization management. Al-Nisman worked in carpentry and participated in several Palestinian series in addition to being active on social media. Assassination : Ali Nisman was assassinated during an Israeli bombing during Operation Flood of Al-Aqsa after his residence in Gaza was targeted . Before his death, he had filmed a video and posted it on social media condemning Israel for its bombing of civilians in the Gaza Strip, and predicted “ more deaths in order to liberate Al-Aqsa .” His death has plunged many of his fans into mourning, with a plethora of social media activists voicing their sorrow over the loss. https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/palestinian-actor-and-activist-ali-nisman-killed-in-gaza-raid-evoking-social-mourning-1.98781234 https://elcinema.com/en/person/2177314/ https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%8A_%D9%86%D8%B3%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86 https://web.archive.org/web/20231014132928/https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/3005201 Image Credit: Source: Eremnews X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

He was active on social media as a Palestinian blogger and was one of the most prominent bloggers. He was active against the Israeli occupation and the Oslo Accords led by the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank . He was one of the most prominent activists during Operation Flood of Al-Aqsa . Al-Nisman was born in Gaza on April 15, 1985. He hails from the northern Gaza City and spent most of his life there. He finished high school and then obtained a bachelor’s degree in business and finance management and a diploma in organization management. Al-Nisman worked in carpentry and participated in several Palestinian series in addition to being active on social media. Assassination : Ali Nisman was assassinated during an Israeli bombing during Operation Flood of Al-Aqsa after his residence in Gaza was targeted . Before his death, he had filmed a video and posted it on social media condemning Israel for its bombing of civilians in the Gaza Strip, and predicted “ more deaths in order to liberate Al-Aqsa .” His death has plunged many of his fans into mourning, with a plethora of social media activists voicing their sorrow over the loss. https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/palestinian-actor-and-activist-ali-nisman-killed-in-gaza-raid-evoking-social-mourning-1.98781234 https://elcinema.com/en/person/2177314/ https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%8A_%D9%86%D8%B3%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86 https://web.archive.org/web/20231014132928/https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/3005201 Image Credit: Source: Eremnews X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: محمد روحي مصطفى الطناني Cameraman at Al Aqsa Channel ("Seraj TV") Killed by IDF targeting of a group of journalists reporting from the Abu Sharkh roundabout in Jabalia on October 9, 2024, during the Israeli siege of Jabalia. His colleague correspondent Tamer Lubbad (تامر لبد) was injured in the same Israeli attack. On the same day the IDF had closed off all access to and from Jabalia and was openly shooting any one trying to leave Jabalia. Journalists who documented those scenes started dubbing the Abu Sharkh roundabout the "Death intersection / roundabout". Mohammed Al-Tanani, a 26-year-old Palestinian journalist and the camera operator for the Hamas-owned Al-Aqsa TV channel, was killed when an Israeli drone fired close to his TV crew covering Israeli forces operations in the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza, according to news reports and his colleague, who spoke to CPJ. The drone strike also injured TV correspondent, Tamer Lubbad. Both Lubbad and Al-Tanani were wearing “Press” vests and helmets, making them clearly identifiable as journalists, according to videos posted online and Lubbad. Lubbad told CPJ via messaging app that “we went to monitor and cover the situation after we learned that the Israeli occupation forces are besieging the Jabalia camp and its residents.” Lubbad said the crew filmed their report at an area close to the camp that was not considered dangerous. “After finishing it, and as we were leaving the area at about 4:30 p.m., a drone fired missiles that hit Mohammed directly, which immediately killed him," Lubbad said. Lubbad told CPJ that “Mohammed Al-Tanani was martyred immediately, as the missile cut through his lower half, and I was hit by shrapnel behind my left shoulder and shrapnel next to my colon.” Lubbad said “repeated and deliberate gunfire” from Israeli forces prevented ambulance crews from reaching Al-Tanani’s body for two hours      .

full_name_ar: عمر خليل عمر البلعاوي Journalist and English teach Omar Khalil Al-Balaawi was shot to death by a live bullet shot by an Israeli drone while standing at the window of his house on Al-Jalaa Street, in Sheikh Radwan, near Gaza City. Omar’s last message on Facebook was “ We are staying steadfast in the north we will only leave to heaven”. He worked as gnlish teacher with HEAL Palestine and the Hands Up Project as "an inspiring leader, cherished by the children he taught, known for spreading joy and enthusiasm in every classroom he entered". He sponsored 'Stories Alive' programme in Gaza. For the past six months he'd been spreading joy and the gift of learning amongst traumatised children in Gaza city      .

full_name_ar: حسن عبد الرحيم علي حمد 19 years-old reporter from northern Gaza who worked notably with Al Jazeera and Anadolu Agency. Killed at home during Israeli onslaught on northern Gaza before dawn October 6. The day and night before, he was bravely documenting the Israeli assault under constant gunfire in pitch darkness, providing key footage documenting the use of artillery shelling and helicopter machine guns against civilian homes. He carried on his journalist mission until his last moments after an almost full 24 hours of reporting and documenting on the ground moving from one place to another, in spite of having a foot/leg injury. At 6 AM, he called a friend of his who used to upload videos on his behalf on X, to send him his last video. After a call that didn’t last more than a few seconds, he said, “There they are, there they are, it’s done,” and hung up. During weeks, Hassan Hamad received threatening messages on WhatsApp, along with several calls from an Israeli officer, instructing him to stop filming Israeli attacks in the Gaza Strip. He didn't comply      .

full_name_ar: وفاء علي عبد ربه العديني Journalist who worked for multiple media and research centers, including as • Writer at The Palestinian Information Center • International Correspondent at The Palestine Chronicle • Author at Fact-File • News Writer at Middle East Monitor • Contributor at BC FM / AM Radio • Founder and manager of 16th October Media Group, a Gaza-based group of young journalists and activists working to convey the Palestinian struggle to international audiences • Activist at International Solidarity Movement Killed along with her husband Munir, her son Tamim, and her daughter Balsam when an Israeli airstrike bombed the family's home around 3 a.m. on September 30th, 2024 in the are al-Baraka area of Deir Al-Balah, in central Gaza. Her other son, Malek, was wounded in the Israeli assault. She is described as a courageous, prominent journalist and activist from Gaza, who worked tirelessly to convey the Palestinian struggle to foreign media through writing, TV interviews, organizing conferences and exhibitions that highlighted Palestinian experiences. During the genocide, she wrote the article "There is no such thing as protective attire for journalists in Gaza" one week after the murder of her colleagues Ismail Al-Ghoul and Rami Al-Rifi. https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20240807-there-is-no-such-thing-as-protective-attire-for-journalists-in-gaza/ In one of her last exchanges on Whatsapp she wrote "I am fine, patient and steadfast." Some biographical element from an article about her work, pre-genocide: - Journalist Wafaa Al-Udaini, who heads the "October 16" team, points out in an interview with "Sanad News Agency" that they seek to make the world able to know the truth about the Israeli aggression against the Palestinians away from forgery and falsification, and continues: "We know that we are walking in a minefield with increasing harassment of everyone who defends Palestine, but we are doing everything we can." - Al-Udaini believes that what she is doing with her team is "a necessary task to convey the truth through a Palestinian voice, in light of the tyranny of the Israeli narrative in its reporting of the current events." - She continues: "It was necessary to have a Palestinian narrative in English that conveys the crimes and aggressions of the Israeli occupation, to convey the truth to the West by putting forward it by the Palestinians." - The team includes 60 male and female volunteers, working in the field of foreign media, and its first steps began with the stage of linguistic and media development in the corridors of libraries and universities and continuous training, away from social networking sites. - "The main objective of establishing the team was to amplify the voice of the Palestinian people, refute the Israeli narrative common in Western society regarding our cause, and put pressure on the peoples who support the occupation by educating these peoples about what is happening in the Palestinian arena." According to Women Press Freedom (@CFWIJ ) : "Wafa fearlessly reported on Gaza’s struggles and mentored young journalists, amplifying the voices of Palestinian people. Her voice for truth and justice will be deeply missed. #WPF vehemently condemns Israel's continued bombardment of Gaza and demands an immediate ceasefire." --- Source: https://alresalah.ps/post/297076/منتدى-الإعلاميين-يندد-باغتيال-الصحفية-وفاء-العديني https://x.com/nournaim88/status/1840632816234549686 https://snd.ps/post/109545/16-أكتوبر-فريق-فلسطيني-يبارز-الرواية-الإسرائيلية-باللغة-الإنجليزي https://x.com/wafa_Gaza https://x.com/ayman_abed93/status/1840693024029814825/photo/1 https://16october.com/about-us/ X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: عبد الله عمر إسماعيل شكشك Journalist for multiple local and Arab media institutions. Killed by an Israeli "quadcopter" that shot him while he was in front of his house in the vicinity of the Kuwaiti Hospital, west of Rafah city. Ambulance crews were not able to retrieve his body immediately due to the presence of Israeli drones, and the risk of being targeted. Abdullah was also supervising charitable initiatives for displaced families in the city of Rafah      .

full_name_ar: حمزة عبد الرحمن مصطفى مرتجى Hamza Murtaja, 27 years old, from Gaza city, was a freelance photojournalist and a co-owner and camera operator for the privately owned Record Media production company, Motasem added that Record Media works with multiple outlets including Reuters, The British Channel 4, Anadolu Agency, Al Jazeera TV, Al Araby TV, and Al Mashhad TV.. He was killed on Augustus 20, 2024 in Israeli massacre at the Mustafa Hafez School in western Gaza City. Murataja, 32, was filming a TV report about the displaced people taking shelter in the school in the al Rimal neighborhood, west of Gaza City, when the airstrike killed him, according to those sources and his brother and colleague at Record Media, Motasem Murtaja, who spoke to CPJ via messaging app from southern Gaza. Motasem Murtaja told CPJ that “Hamza was wearing a helmet and a press vest” at the time, adding that Record Media is committed to safety requirements for their journalists and “we agreed to minimize the number of journalists on the ground reporting to minimize the human loss if the places we report from were hit.” Hamza and Motasem’s older brother, Yaser Murtaja, was a photojournalist who died in 2018 after he was shot by Israeli forces while covering a protest. “Yaser was like a father to us, and Hamza was like a support and partner to me,” Motasem told CPJ. “There is no doubt that this is a difficult and great loss, but our hope is in God, and His compensation is greater.” Motasem added, “Hamza and Yaser are now martyrs, Bilal [their brother] and I are the only ones left. We are all journalists.” Hamza Murtaja was the father of two children: Omar, 4, and Yaser, 6 months. Yaser was named after his uncle, the murdered journalist, and was born during the Israel-Gaza war, on the same day Yaser was killed. According to Motasem Murtaja, Hamza had not met his son Yaser. Record Media was established in 2019 by Motasem and Hamza Murtaja after their brother’s shares in Ain Media were sold to Roshdi Sarraj, a photojournalist who was killed in an Israeli airstrike in October 2023. “We established it with one camera, but we were able to cooperate with major media institutions,” Motasem told CPJ. The IDF said in an August 28 letter to CPJ that "Murtaja was an operative in the military branch of Hamas and was struck while staying in a Hamas command and control center that was embedded and hidden by the Hamas terrorist organization inside the ‘Mustafa Khaft’ School compound in Gaza City." The letter did not provide details to support this claim      .

name_en: Tamim Abu Muammar تميم أبو معمر
full_name_ar: تميم أحمد أبو معمر Palestinian journalist and editor for the Palestinian Broadcasting Corporation’s “Voice of Palestine" The Palestinian Journalists Syndicate (PJS) Statement: The PJS condemnes the killing of journalists Tamim Muammar and Abdullah Al-Sousi by Israeli occupation forces in the Gaza Strip, describing it as "a new crime in the context of the systematic targeting of journalists by the occupation." According to the photojournalist Hassan Eslayeh: "This photo was collected by fellow journalist and editor of the official Voice of Palestine Radio, Tamim Muammar, with his wife and all of his children. Tamim rose with his wife and three of his children, and only Abdul Rahman, who is 7 years old, and Yahya, who is 11 years old, remain. Yesterday, their home in Khan Yunis was targeted by Tamim’s sons, who were: Shams (13), Salam (15) and Mis (4) According to the Al-Hadath newspaper correspondent in Gaza: "The two journalists, Tamim Muammar, who works for Palestine TV, and Abdullah Al-Soussi, who works for Al-Aqsa TV, were martyred in two separate raids in Khan Yunis, along with a number of their children and relatives." According to Palestine Today : "Journalists Tamim Muammar from Voice of Palestine Radio and Abdullah Al-Soussi from Al-Aqsa TV, along with a number of their children and relatives, were killed in two separate airstrikes on Khan Younis" According to Hakeam : "The martyred journalist Tamim Muammar at the top and the picture below of the nurse Abdul Rahman Yahya Muammar were killed during the bombing of a house in the Tahlia area in Khan Yunis." X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

full_name_ar: إسماعيل ماهر خميس الغول • Al-Jazeera correspondent in Gaza City since late October 2023. Ismail graduated in journalism and media studies from the Islamic University of Gaza. He worked for two newspapers Falasteen and Al-Risala prior to joining Al-Jazeera. • Ismail was instrumental in documenting and uncovering some of the major Israeli massacres including the murder of Hind Rajab, her family and paramedics, the Flour massacre, and the Al-Shifa hospital siege and total destruction, during which he was detained and abused by the IDF before being released on March 18th. • Ismail was murdered in a targeted airstrike on his car along with his colleague cameraman Rami Al-Rifi, where both were gruesomely beheaded. • His colleague Islam Badr who works for Al Araby TV recounted how the assassination unfolded: Journalists were reporting on the assassination of Ismail Haniyeh on the same day in front of the latter's residence, conducting interviews. The area was situated a considerable distance from active combat zones. Drones were flying overhead. The initial strike impacted the coverage area. Journalists evacuated using two vehicles: one belonging to Ismail and another from a national press organization. The vehicles proceeded in opposite directions due to the hazardous situation. The second strike directly hit Ismail's vehicle. Islam Badr asserted that this was unequivocally intentional. --- Sources: https://x.com/Qadeyah1/status/1850571641517998169 X Stop Murdering Journalists is a project of Databases for Palestine    .

name_en: Muhammad Abu Armana محمد أبو عرمانة
full_name_ar: محمد منهل أبو عرمانة Armanah, journalist at Palestine Now News Agency, was killed in an Israeli airstrike that struck tents sheltering displaced civilians in the al-Mawasi area west of Khan Yunis in the southern Gaza Strip on July 13, 2024, during the event that became known as the Mawasi massacre. The Israeli military said the strikes were intended to target Mohammed Deif. Beginning at approximately 10:30 a.m., a series of Israeli airstrikes hit a compound near the al-Nas Junction in al-Mawasi. Initial reports identified at least 55 civilians killed, with later estimates placing the death toll at around 90 and as many as 150, while approximately 300 people were reported injured. By the evening, the Gaza Ministry of Health stated that around half of those killed were women and children, and that dozens of women and children were among the wounded. The strikes also killed at least three civil defence workers and one journalist, while injuring a photographer. Local reports described multiple strikes occurring in rapid succession, with Al Jazeera reporting "five bombs and five missiles," making it difficult to determine which victims were killed in each individual strike. The casualty figures refer to the combined toll from the entire series of strikes. According to the French independant Media, Mediapart, just one month after the death of her husband, who was killed in an Israeli airstrike, Alia shared on Facebook the profound sense of emptiness that has taken hold of her : “The death of your partner means becoming disabled for the rest of your life — looking at everything around you and finding it colorless, living with half a heart, half a soul, half your ambitions and half a body. It means losing the one person who understood your spirit, the embrace that held you and made you feel safe.” On July 13, her husband, Mohamed Manhal Abou Armana, was killed by an Israeli drone strike while documenting the devastation left behind by an attack on the Al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis. The strike killed several displaced Palestinians who had fled the bombardments and sought refuge in tents set up along the southern Gaza coast, an area designated as a humanitarian zone. The 32-year-old Palestinian journalist was taking photographs of the victims for the local pro-Hamas news agency Palestine Now when he was himself killed      .
